content:
Rafael Mendes: Seeing p95 latency spike + some 5xx on Hosted us-east-1, top routes are /v1/chat/completions for `llama-3.1-70b` pool. Started ~10 min ago. Anyone aware of a config push? :eyes:

incident-bot: Incident #INC-1842 created by @Rafael Mendes
Severity: SEV2
Service: inference-hosted
Region: us-east-1
Links: Grafana https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/hosted-inference/overview?var-region=us-east-1 | Runbook https://confluence.redwoodinference.net/display/SRE/Hosted+Inference+Oncall

Neha Kapoor: I’m on too. What changed right before the spike? Check optimize config + runtime deploys.

Rafael Mendes: No deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot. Looking at config-change logs… don’t see a single “event” stream (this is the gap we talked about). I’m going to diff the live Optimize config vs yesterday’s known-good.

Allison Grant: Dashboard for correlation (latency + error vs config knobs):
- https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/optimize-change-health/hosted-config-change-health?var-region=us-east-1
Also Honeycomb trace sample (timeouts): https://ui.honeycomb.io/redwood/datasets/inference/trace?query=route%3D%2Fv1%2Fchat%2Fcompletions%20status%3E%3D500

deploy-bot: No production deploys detected for service `control-plane` or `runtime-scheduler` in us-east-1 in last 90m.

Sean Gallagher: If it’s config related, goal is mitigation in minutes. If manual rollback is messy, pick the safest “known-good” from last week and hard-revert. Document every step here.

Rafael Mendes: OK. Step 1: Identify suspect change.
- In Grafana, spike coincides with GPU saturation + batch queue depth.
- `optimize.batching.max_batch_tokens` might have been raised.

Rafael Mendes: Pulling current config from control plane (manual):
`rwctl optimize config get --scope hosted/us-east-1 --model llama-3.1-70b --route chat_completions > /tmp/optimize_live.json`

Rafael Mendes: I don’t have a “history” endpoint (yet). Looking for last known-good in the #eng-runtime pinned snippet from last incident… found older file in SRE bucket.

Neha Kapoor: Do we have a previous snapshot in the incident doc? Maybe from the Oct regression.

Rafael Mendes: Yep, found in “INC-1769 notes” (Google Drive). Copying local:
`gsutil cp gs://redwood-sre-prod/optimize-config-snapshots/us-east-1/llama-3.1-70b/chat_completions_2024-10-28.json /tmp/optimize_known_good.json`

Rafael Mendes: Step 2: Diff locally.
`jd -set /tmp/optimize_known_good.json /tmp/optimize_live.json | head`
Differences I see (relevant):
- `batching.max_batch_tokens`: 8192 -> 16384
- `batching.max_concurrent_sequences`: 96 -> 160
- `cache.prefix_cache.enabled`: true -> false
- `quant.profile`: `int8_kv` -> `fp16`

Sofia Ivanova: 160 concurrent seq + 16k tokens is pretty aggressive for that pool, especially with mixed context lengths. Would explain queueing + tail.

Mateo Alvarez: Also: flipping prefix cache off will raise compute on common prefixes, will inflate latency and can trigger OOM if the batching params are high.

Omar El-Sayed: If quant profile changed to fp16 at the same time, memory pressure goes way up. That combo is exactly “bad day.”

Rafael Mendes: Step 3: Manual rollback attempt (since no one-click rollback exists).
I’m going to apply the known-good snapshot back to the control plane.
Command (dry-run doesn’t exist either, so doing cautious apply):
`rwctl optimize config apply --scope hosted/us-east-1 --model llama-3.1-70b --route chat_completions --file /tmp/optimize_known_good.json --reason "INC-1842 mitigate latency"`

Chloe Martin: Heads up: apply is not atomic across clusters; it fans out per cell. Watch for partial propagation / split brain.

Rafael Mendes: Yup. Step 4: Verify propagation status (manual).
No UI. Checking runtime config endpoint per cell:
- cell-a: `curl -s http://runtime-cell-a.us-east-1/admin/config/optimize?model=llama-3.1-70b | jq '.batching.max_batch_tokens,.batching.max_concurrent_sequences,.cache.prefix_cache.enabled,.quant.profile'`
- cell-b: same

Rafael Mendes: Results:
- cell-a updated (8192/96/cache on/int8_kv)
- cell-b still old (16384/160/cache off/fp16)

Neha Kapoor: That’s the nightmare. Can we force refresh / restart on cell-b without taking everything down?

Mateo Alvarez: There’s a runtime “config poll” interval; sometimes it wedges. You can hit the admin reload endpoint:
`POST /admin/reload_config` (auth required). Or bounce scheduler pods for that cell.

Rafael Mendes: Step 5: Attempt forced reload.
`curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_ADMIN" http://runtime-cell-b.us-east-1/admin/reload_config`
Response: `{"ok":true}`

Rafael Mendes: Re-checking config… still old. :/

Sofia Ivanova: If reload didn’t take, scheduler might be stuck on old config due to failed parse. Any logs?

Allison Grant: Cell-b logs panel:
https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/explore?orgId=1&left=%7B%22datasource%22:%22loki-prod%22,%22queries%22:%5B%7B%22expr%22:%22%7Bcluster%3D%5C%22hosted-us-east-1-cell-b%5C%22,service%3D%5C%22runtime-scheduler%5C%22%7D%20%7C%3D%20%5C%22optimize%5C%22%22%7D%5D%7D

Rafael Mendes: Found error in scheduler logs on cell-b:
`optimize_config_apply failed: validation error: max_concurrent_sequences 96 below min for this pool (min=128)`
Wait what? That’s backwards. It’s rejecting the lower value.

Mateo Alvarez: That “min=128” sounds like a new guardrail from earlier this week. It’s not in docs/runbook.

Sean Gallagher: We need to mitigate now. What’s the safe config that *passes* current validator but reduces blast radius?

Sofia Ivanova: For that pool: keep `max_concurrent_sequences` at 128 (if validator insists), reduce tokens back to 8192, and turn prefix cache back on. Quant profile back to int8_kv if allowed.

Rafael Mendes: Step 6: Create “compromise rollback” that passes validation.
Editing /tmp/optimize_compromise.json:
- max_batch_tokens: 8192
- max_concurrent_sequences: 128
- cache.prefix_cache.enabled: true
- quant.profile: int8_kv

Rafael Mendes: Applying compromise to cell-b scope (same scope applies to all cells though… but cell-a already on 96; will move to 128, acceptable).
`rwctl optimize config apply --scope hosted/us-east-1 --model llama-3.1-70b --route chat_completions --file /tmp/optimize_compromise.json --reason "INC-1842 rollback (validator-compatible)"`

Devon Price: If you want, I can post status in incident channel + link the exact command for audit trail. (We really need audit events here.)

Rafael Mendes: Please do.

incident-bot: Update from @Rafael Mendes
Action: Manual Optimize config rollback in progress (rwctl apply). Noted partial propagation + validator mismatch. Monitoring p95 latency and 5xx.
Incident channel: #inc-1842

Rafael Mendes: Step 7: Verify propagation again.
Now:
- cell-a: 8192/128/cache on/int8_kv
- cell-b: 8192/128/cache on/int8_kv

Allison Grant: Metrics trend: p95 is coming down (was ~2.8s, now ~1.6s), error rate down from 1.2% to 0.3%. Still above baseline though.

Omar El-Sayed: If quant profile change triggered cache invalidation, you might have a warmup period. But prefix cache back on should help quickly.

Neha Kapoor: Can we confirm no other routes/models got the same change?

Rafael Mendes: Checking top offenders list… `llama-3.1-8b` seems fine. The spike is localized to 70b chat pool.

Sean Gallagher: Capture postmortem notes now: manual rollback was slow because (1) no config history, (2) no diff/preview, (3) propagation not atomic, (4) validator behavior blocked known-good config.

Rafael Mendes: Agreed. Writing follow-ups here.

Rafael Mendes: Follow-up tasks (please react/assign):
1) Need immutable version history + “rollback to version” so I’m not grepping old incident docs for JSON (:facepalm:).
2) Safe-apply should provide preflight validation with explicit errors (including guardrails like min/max) BEFORE applying to any cell.
3) Rollback must be atomic per scope or at least show per-cell rollout status to avoid split brain.
4) Audit log event emitted for apply/rollback attempt (who/what/where/reason) + correlation id.
5) Validator bug/UX: it claimed 96 < min=128 (new rule?) but we have no visibility. Should be documented + surfaced in UI.

Dylan Brooks: :thumbsup: this is exactly why we’re doing the project. I’ll open Linear tickets for (1)-(4). Chloe can help confirm the validator rule + how to surface it.

Chloe Martin: I’ll look into the validator rule set and why it thinks min=128. Might be pool-specific config we forgot to update in SRE runbook.

Mateo Alvarez: On runtime side, we should expose “current applied config version/hash” and last successful apply timestamp in `/admin/status` so on-call can verify quickly.

Allison Grant: Also: add a Grafana annotation when config changes (even if manual) so we can correlate without eyeballing. Right now we have nothing.

Neha Kapoor: Status check: are we back within SLO?

Rafael Mendes: Current:
- p95: 1.1s (baseline ~0.9s)
- 5xx: 0.08%
- GPU util down, queue depth normalizing
I’m going to keep watching for 15 min then downgrade monitoring.

Sean Gallagher: Please paste the final compromise config in the incident doc and pin it in #eng-oncall for now.

Rafael Mendes: Pasting here for record:
```json
{
  "batching": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 8192,
    "max_concurrent_sequences": 128,
    "target_batch_latency_ms": 18
  },
  "cache": {
    "prefix_cache": {"enabled": true, "max_entries": 20000}
  },
  "quant": {
    "profile": "int8_kv"
  },
  "routing": {
    "fallback_enabled": true,
    "fallback_model": "llama-3.1-70b-instruct"
  }
}
```

Devon Price: Posted in #inc-1842 with the command + config snippet and added a reminder that this is not an audited workflow yet.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-1842 status update
Mitigation applied. Monitoring for recovery.
Owner: @Rafael Mendes

Rafael Mendes: Last note: this took ~25 minutes end-to-end because of partial propagation + validator surprise. Our MTTR target is single-digit minutes. This feature can’t land soon enough.

Neha Kapoor: +1. Thanks for driving. Let’s make sure the PRD explicitly covers: per-cell status, preflight, and a rollback path that does not get blocked by newly introduced validators without an override for on-call.

Sean Gallagher: (Action item) I’ll email SRE leadership summary + add this thread link as evidence for the “Safe apply + rollback” initiative.

Rafael Mendes: Closing loop: latency stable. I’m stepping down from incident but leaving it in monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-1842 moved to Monitoring by @Rafael Mendes
